dedupe_keys.name: sciesmex space weather now mexican space weather service data

description: The Mexican Space Weather Service, SCiESMEX, at the Institute of Geophysics of the National Autonomous University of Mexico, publishes a Space Weather Now page with real-time observations from UNAM instruments and from international public sources. The UNAM RICE network data includes interplanetary scintillation from the Mexican Array Radio Telescope (MEXART), the Callisto-MEXART radio spectrograph and its light curve, the Teoloyucan Magnetic Observatory and the cosmic ray observatory, and the page adds NASA SDO solar images, NOAA GOES X-ray and proton flux, the Kyoto Dst geomagnetic index and NASA JPL total electron content maps, each with a short explanation of what it shows. Access is free to view; the site states all rights reserved and gives no open licence. Caveats: the page is a real-time display, and the international series are credited to their original providers. Coverage is Mexico for the UNAM instruments, with global solar and geomagnetic context. It supports hazard exposure analysis of space weather for power grids, radio communications and GNSS in Mexico; related records are the NICT space weather forecast, Space Weather Canada and the Tromsø Geophysical Observatory data.
